questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.question_text: Carbon monoxide poisoning: cherry-red color of skin is due to?
questions.explanation: CO poisoning: HbCO (cherry-pink/red discoloration of mucous membranes, lividity, organs). CO has 240x affinity for Hb vs O2. Treatment: 100% O2 (hyperbaric in severe). CO also binds cytochrome oxidase.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.question_text: Diatom test (Incinerator test) is done for?
questions.explanation: Diatom test (Getler/Owen test): siliceous diatom shells found in bone marrow/viscera confirm antemortem drowning (diatoms can only enter circulation when heart is beating). Speciation confirms water source.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.question_text: Rigor mortis: sequence of development?
questions.explanation: Rigor mortis: follows Nysten's law — starts in jaw/neck, then trunk, then lower limbs. Onset: 1-2 hours. Maximum: 12 hours. Passes off: 36-48 hours. Due to ATP depletion → actin-myosin cross-linking.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.question_text: Age of consent for medical procedures in India (IPC/BNS)?
questions.explanation: Age of consent in India: 18 years. Below 18: guardian's consent required (exception: emergency, mature minor doctrine). Under POCSO Act, all sexual activity with <18 is criminal regardless of consent.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.question_text: Post-mortem caloricity (temperature rise after death)?

options.B: Seen in strychnine poisoning and status epilepticus deaths (heat generated from muscle activity)

questions.explanation: PM caloricity: rise in body temperature after death. Seen in: strychnine poisoning (convulsions continuing after death), tetanus, status epilepticus, typhoid, pontine hemorrhage.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.question_text: Putrefaction: first sign?

options.B: Greenish discoloration of right iliac fossa (cecum area)

questions.explanation: Putrefaction: first sign is greenish discoloration of right iliac fossa (cecal bacteria: H2S + Hb → green sulfhemoglobin). Then marbling, bloating, skin slippage. Rate influenced by temperature and environment.
